newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended weaker on Thursday as market negativity greeted the release of a host of key economic indicators and triggered widespread demand for dollars, dealers said.
The local currency was last quoted at 4.4650/4680 against the dollar after trading between a 4.4680 bid and 4.4350 bid on the day and from 4.4360/90 overnight.
Dollar demand by local importers and some offshore banks as well as foreign disinvestment in domestic gilts helped to depress the market, dealers said.
Sentiment was dented by January trade and CPI data which came in at the worst-end of market expectations, dealers said.

South Africa registered a trade surplus of 517.2 million rand in January -- below market expectations of an 817 million rand surplus, while January consumer inflation rose 9.4 percent -- the top end of economists' range.
"The market wasn't impressed with the (trade) figure -- we were looking for 800 million but it came in at 517.20 million. A lot of guys had the wind taken out of their sails a bit," a dealer said.
GDP, the third indicator which was released during trading hours, came in at 3.3 percent in the fourth quarter and was in line with market expectations.
Dealers said the demand for dollars, which continued throughout much of the day, drew Reserve Bank support around the 4.44 level.
In the afternoon session it moved to smooth liquidity as the currency continued to weaken.
"He's been showing prices all day and moving them up. He's keeping it as stable as possible. Nothing's really been unorderly at all," one dealer said.
Traders said the disappointing indicators had also affected the bond market.

Bonds had opened weaker in the early session after a selloff on U.S. Treasuries following Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning that stock prices may have risen too far and hints the Federal Reserve may hike U.S. interest rates.
"Invariably whenever America sneezes the rest of the world gets a cold," one trader said.
The first of the batch of economic data -- the trade balance -- was released at 0800 GMT, followed by the CPI at 1100 GMT.

"The trade balance and CPI were both on the worse side of the range -- the trade figures were the worst because there were unofficial rumours that it would be a good figure and instead it came in worse than expected," one trader said.
The indicators had introduced an element of uncertainty into the market, the trader said.
"Everybody is a bit nervous especially with the figures which came out today. I think it will all depend on the budget now," he added.
Trade on the day was mainly driven by local jobbers and smaller overseas players.
The benchmark R150 was last at 14.60 percent after reaching an intraday high of 14.62 percent and from 14.52 percent overnight.
Bond Exchange statistics show foreigners bought a net 107.81 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 245.80 million on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.3 billion rand from 7.3 billion rand on Tuesday.
Against the crosses the rand was last quoted at 7.2674/2767 against sterling from 7.2565/2659 on Wednesday and at 0.3774/3778 from 0.3780/3784 marks previously.
On the money market, rates held unchanged between 16.50 and 16.70 percent. The 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.927 million rand on Wednesday from 10.139 million rand on Tuesday.
-- Juliette Saunders, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
